beats.caption: This is <v>the most beautiful</v> sunset in the world!

say: Faster than me. The most beautiful sunset in the world. Mia is comparing things. We do this every day, so let's learn comparatives and superlatives.
By the end, you'll know the rules, the irregular forms, and the mistakes to avoid.

data.heading: Comparative or superlative?
rows: Whiskers is the fastest cat in the village.

say: First, the idea.
We use the comparative to compare two things: Whiskers is faster than Mia.
We use the superlative for one thing in a group of three or more: Whiskers is the fastest cat in the village.
Look at Whiskers jump! He's quicker than a bird, and braver than any other cat.
beats.caption: He's <v>quicker than</v> a bird!

say: Short adjectives, with one syllable, add e r and e s t.
Tall, taller than, the tallest.
If it ends in e, just add r or s t: nice, nicer, the nicest.
One vowel and one consonant? Double it: big, bigger, the biggest.
Hot, hotter, the hottest. Muscat is hotter than London.
Adjectives ending in y change the y to i.
Happy, happier, the happiest.
Easy, easier, the easiest.
Funny, funnier, the funniest.
Longer adjectives use more and the most. We don't change the adjective.
Beautiful, more beautiful than, the most beautiful.
Expensive, more expensive than, the most expensive.
Interesting, more interesting than, the most interesting.
And three irregular ones. You must learn them by heart.
Good, better, the best.
Bad, worse, the worst.
Far, farther or further, the farthest.

beats.caption: This is <v>the most beautiful</v> sunset in the world!

data.heading: Saying it naturally
data.tip: Put your tongue between your teeth for th

say: A quick pronunciation tip.
Than is weak and short: taller than. Better than.
The is also weak: the best. The biggest.
And the e r ending is a soft sound: bigger, faster, older.
For the t h sound, put your tongue between your teeth. Than. The.

data.heading: Equal: as ... as
data.rule: as + adjective + as / not as ... as
examples: Mia is <v>as tall as</v> her friend.
Whiskers is <v>not as big as</v> a dog.
Today is <v>not as hot as</v> yesterday.
data.note: not as big as = smaller than

say: When two things are the same, use as, adjective, as.
Mia is as tall as her friend.
For a difference, say not as, adjective, as: Whiskers is not as big as a dog.
Today is not as hot as yesterday.
So not as big as means smaller than.
From the hill, Mia can see the whole valley. This is the highest place in the village, and the river looks smaller than a ribbon.
beats.caption: This is <v>the highest</v> place in the village.

data.heading: Questions
pairs: Which is <v>bigger</v>, the sun or the moon?
Who is <v>the oldest</v> in your family?

say: Some useful questions.
Which is bigger, the sun or the moon? The sun is much bigger. Notice much, it makes the difference stronger.
Who is the oldest in your family? My grandma is the oldest.
What's the best film you've ever seen?

beats.caption: Is the river <v>deeper than</v> the lake?

data.heading: Common mistakes (Arabic speakers)
rows: He is more tall than me.
He is the tallest in the class.

say: Now the common mistakes.
He is more tall than me. Tall is short, so: he is taller than me.
She is more better. Better is already a comparative: she is better.
It's the most big house. It's the biggest house.
Muscat is hotter from Dubai. We use than: Muscat is hotter than Dubai.
He is tallest in class. Don't forget the: he is the tallest in the class.

data.q: An elephant is ___ than a horse.
This is the ___ book in the library.

beats.say_answer: Most interesting. It's a long adjective.

data.q: My cold is ___ today than yesterday.
Mia is as tall ___ her friend.
Sunday is the ___ day of the week.

say: Let's remember. Comparatives compare two things, with than. Superlatives pick one from a group, with the.
Short adjectives add e r and e s t, y becomes i, and long adjectives use more and the most.
And learn the irregulars: good, better, best. Bad, worse, worst.
